# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

   3|     Touching intervals, e.g. (1,3) and (3,5), merge into (1,5).
   4|     Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""

content: All tests pass and the sanity checks confirm correct behavior: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, and edge cases (empty, single, containment) work.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py`: the merge condition `start < last_end` was changed to `start <= merged[-1][1]` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. (1,3) and (3,5)) merge into (1,5), and the input is now sorted before processing so unsorted input is handled correctly. Rewrote the loop to iterate over the fully sorted list, appending a new interval when it doesn't overlap/touch the last merged one and extending it (with max end) otherwise. Verified with the existing test suite (2 tests pass) plus manual checks for unsorted, empty, single, and containment cases.
